assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active-matter hydrodynamics established a new class of nonequilibrium statistical physics: the Vicsek flocking model, the Toner-Tu continuum theory with long-range order in two dimensions despite the Mermin-Wagner obstruction, and the hydrodynamics of orientationally ordered active fluids. The concepts (giant number fluctuations, motility-induced phenomena, anomalous scaling) are original, clear and have spread to bacterial suspensions, cytoskeletal gels, swarming animals and synthetic swimmers. From my own vantage in stochastic and complex-systems physics this is a genuine, conceptually unified field.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names cover the numerical minimal model (Vicsek), the field theory and renormalization-group treatment (Toner and Tu), and the hydrodynamic formulation of active ordered fluids (Ramaswamy and collaborators). Yuhai Tu is not on the credited list, so the Toner-Tu theory would be recognised through Toner alone; this is a real credit question but a workable three-person configuration exists.
assessment.maturity: About three decades of theory, quantitative experiments on vibrated granular rods, colloidal rollers and bacterial turbulence, and a very large community. Timing is good; the main residual concern is that some predictions (exact exponents) are confirmed only in a few systems.
uncertainties: Omission of Yuhai Tu and of other early contributors (Toner-Tu 1995 was joint) leaves an attribution asymmetry.
Quantitative experimental tests of the full Toner-Tu exponents remain limited and partly debated.
Uncertain whether the committee would regard this as physics of living matter or as mainstream statistical physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a large and productive field with tunable correlated and topological states. The discovery is clear, original and conceptually rich, connecting to strongly correlated electrons and, for me, to complex many-body behaviour in a highly controllable platform.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Pairing theory with experiment is clean. Cory Dean, Yuan Cao and others contributed substantially but the three credited names form a defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many labs and by multiple techniques within a few years; the field is very active, though the nature of the superconducting pairing is not settled. Recognition would be somewhat early but the impact is already large.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of superconductivity and the full phase diagram are unsettled.
Reproducibility and sample-dependence (twist-angle disorder) remain active issues.
Prior theoretical antecedents (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) raise an unresolved credit question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 construction of two-dimensional conformal field theory (BPZ) turned scale-invariant critical phenomena into an exactly solvable framework with infinite-dimensional symmetry. It underlies the classification of 2D universality classes, minimal models, the Kosterlitz-Thouless and Ising critical exponents, string worldsheet theory and boundary critical phenomena. As a statistical physicist I regard it as deeply original and permanent, with a long and robust record of application.
assessment.attribution: The Belavin-Polyakov-Zamolodchikov paper is the unambiguous founding work, and the three names match it exactly, giving a naturally clean credit configuration. Friedan, Qiu and Shenker, and Cardy, made important follow-up contributions but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of consequences, with experimental confirmations in critical exponents and exact lattice results; maturity is not in doubt. The only question is whether the prize has deferred it because it is mathematical and theoretical.
uncertainties: Part of the work lies near mathematical physics, and the committee may judge direct experimental connection less decisive.
Polyakov's other work (gauge/gravity, instantons) overlaps with other candidates and could complicate a split.
I cannot independently verify the current status or availability of all three living laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organisation as liquid-liquid phase separation, with P granules and nucleoli behaving as liquid droplets. The physics is that of soft matter and nonequilibrium thermodynamics, including active and driven droplets, and it changes how cell biologists think about compartmentalisation without membranes. It is interdisciplinary, conceptually clear, and has a very large following.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman supplied the decisive 2009 P-granule experiments; Jülicher gave the physical theory of droplet dynamics and active condensates. This is a plausible three-person split, though other contributors (Rosen, Fawzi, Pappu, Parry, others) shaped the field, so credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Rapid and wide uptake, but there is continuing debate about which cellular structures are true thermodynamic phase separation versus other assemblies, and about physiological relevance; as a physics prize it may be early.
uncertainties: Controversy over whether in vivo condensates are equilibrium phase-separated phases.
Whether the committee views this as physics or as a biology/chemistry prize.
Competing credit claims across cell biology, polymer physics and biochemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the Jaksch-Zoller Hubbard proposal and the Mott-insulator observation to quantum gas microscopes, supplies a highly controlled platform for strongly correlated many-body physics. It realises the statistical-mechanics models I work with and has produced precise tests of lattice models. The idea is original and impactful.
assessment.attribution: Bloch is the leading experimentalist, Zoller and Cirac the leading theorists. Greiner (Mott insulator and microscope) and Hänsch and Esslinger overlap; the four-name credit list is capped at three, which forces an exclusion of Greiner.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of progress, and strong independent confirmation, but the 2025 and nearby frontier work is still rapidly developing; some overlap with the already recognised BEC and laser-cooling prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidates crediting Cirac and Zoller for trapped-ion and atom-based quantum computation, which affects how credit can be allocated.
Choosing among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and the theorists is contested.
The line between platform development and a discrete discovery is not sharp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced time-reversal-protected topological phases, with predicted and then observed helical edge states in HgTe wells. The concept restructured band theory and is of lasting importance for condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Molenkamp led the HgTe observation. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased) predicted the HgTe effect and 3D topological insulators involved Fu, Hasan, Moore and others, so a three-name selection leaves some unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and bulk 3D materials; timing is good but the prize may have a credit problem.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu, Hasan, Moore, and the death of Shoucheng Zhang.
Overlap with the quantum anomalous Hall candidates.
Graphene QSH gap is too small for observation as proposed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems (Evans-Searles, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski, Crooks) give exact relations for entropy production and work in far-from-equilibrium systems, extending the second law to small stochastic systems. This is central to modern stochastic thermodynamics, with experiments on colloids, RNA pulling and single-electron devices.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed among Evans, Cohen, Searles, Gallavotti, Jarzynski and Crooks; the three credited names exclude Cohen, Searles and Crooks, so any three-person selection is partly arbitrary. I choose these three as the supplied set.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed experimentally, with mature theoretical foundations, but the community has not converged on a single canonical discovery and the conceptual gap to a prize-sized discovery is arguable.
uncertainties: Strong attribution ambiguity; omitted contributors have comparable claims.
Whether it is a single discovery or a family of related results.
I am drawing partly on my own field, so I may be biased in favour of stochastic thermodynamics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength proposal and subsequent realisation, brought fractional frequency uncertainties to the 1e-18 level, enabling tests of relativity, geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The invention is clear and of lasting metrological impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic wavelength lattice concept and Ye led the leading clock realisations; the two-name configuration is clean, though the Hall and Hänsch prize (2005) and ion-clock work by Wineland overlap in the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation from multiple laboratories; the second redefinition has not yet happened, so recognition could be considered either timely or slightly early.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes.
Applications such as redefinition of the second are still pending.
Possible additional credit claims for Pierre Lemonde and others who are not in the credited list.
